races.name: Burke's Clonbur 3-Y-O Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Divine Believer
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's hold-up juvenile showed limited flat form in soft and good ground but steps up to 2m2f over hurdles for the first time; the step in trip is the key question, and from the rear of a 16-runner field she needs the pace to develop properly to be produced with any impact.

runners_data.name: Another Day Done
runners_data.note: Anthony McCann's runner won on Standard ground at 8f and has placed at that level, but its true inclination is to race from behind — the field's congestion means it is shown in midfield rather than the back, and that positional compromise tempers its realistic chance of landing this despite the STYLE_FIT suggesting ability.

runners_data.name: Chairmanforlife
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's prominent racer has struggled in larger fields at Leopardstown and Naas but the drop to this level of maiden hurdle and a more strongly-run race would help; races close to the pace which suits Scenario A or D.

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's gelding won on Soft at 10f on the Flat and has placed at 17 and 17 furlongs over hurdles, suggesting this trip on this ground is genuinely within his compass; he wears a tongue-strap and is ridden by a 5lb claimer but the profile fits a prominent racer in a steadily-run race.

runners_data.name: Point Star
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's midfield type has only one run to his name, finishing fourth from 18 runners at Galway on Good — very limited data but no obvious going concern; the 7lb claimer Thomas O'Connor adds to the uncertainty in a big field.

runners_data.name: Armillary
runners_data.note: Miss Tara Lee Cogan's unknown quantity — no public form, no days-since-last-run data, lightly raced flag active — this is a genuine dark horse with style unknown; Harry Sexton (7lb claimer) adds further risk.

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's three-year-old has three hurdles runs to its name with a best of eighth, and its natural inclination is to race from the back; the packed rear of this field means it will likely be placed further forward than ideal, which the STYLE_FIT discount reflects, and its form offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Step By Step
runners_data.note: Another unknown with no public form and headgear (hood) already deployed at this early stage; Aidan Anthony Howard has a small yard but recent winner in the 14-day stats, and the hood may be a market indicator if support materialises.

runners_data.name: Wills History
runners_data.note: Brian McMahon's debutant with no known form — style unknown, no going record, and a 5lb claimer in Calum Hogan; treat as a market-mover watch only.

runners_data.name: We're Out Of Aces
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's unraced runner carries the weight of a powerful yard — T14 of 4/33 shows the stable in decent form — but with no public form, this remains a significant unknown; any market move should be flagged as a danger.

runners_data.name: Bell Ex Too
runners_data.note: R P Cody's gelding has five hurdles runs, never better than fifth, and naturally races from the back; squeezed into midfield by the field's hold-up congestion, its true position is the rear and its best run came on Soft at 9f, so the trip and going combination is at least not a concern.

runners_data.name: Montevetro
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's sole confirmed pace-setter, who placed on Standard and placed twice at 10f on Flat, steps up significantly in trip; he sets the tactical shape of the entire race and if the ground saps his stamina in the final half-mile the race opens up for closers, but with no rival to force a hot pace he has the advantage of controlling the tempo.

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's hold-up type has mixed Flat form including a second at 10f on Good, and wears a hood; the 7lb claimer Alix Balfe rode only six days ago, suggesting a busy schedule, and the horse needs pace to be produced from the back of a traffic-heavy field.

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's hold-up runner has placed at 14f on Good and has a consistent placing profile in midfield at this stage; no jockey listed publicly, no headgear concern, but needs a genuinely-run race to exploit a late run from the rear.

runners_data.name: Matada
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's hold-up type has three runs, best of twelfth, and has been off 111 days — the longest absence in the field; the return from a lengthy break in a 16-runner maiden is a significant risk factor regardless of stable form.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's gelding wears a hood (first time headgear), has six runs with a best of sixth, and raced only six days ago — the quick turnaround and new headgear are the headline angles; races from the back and needs the pace to develop to be competitive.

races.paceDynamic: Montevetro is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-horse field and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop on Good to Yielding ground over 2m2f — a genuinely sustainable pace scenario rather than a pressured one. Behind him, the field is dominated by hold-up types, though Camp Verde, Bell Ex Too, and Another Day Done are all genuine hold-up horses that have been pushed forward on the pace map because the rear of the field is congested; in practice, several of these will be forced wider and slightly more prominent than their natural style, creating a bunched midfield rather than a clean split of pace and closers. Divine Believer, the Strand Scorecard selection, races from the back and will need Montevetro to either set enough of a gallop to create a genuine test or for the race to develop late, which is plausible if the ground rides on the softer side of Good to Yielding. This race shape — a lone leader controlling pace in front of a cluttered hold-up division — most clearly favours horses that can travel prominently or in the first third of midfield and deliver a sustained run from two out, rather than those relying on a truly strong pace to produce them from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Montevetro Controls, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro leads at a steady clip and the winner comes from midfield as hold-up types fail to get a strong enough gallop.
scenarios.body: Montevetro sets a comfortable tempo that suits prominent and mid-division horses who can improve from the second last without needing a true end-to-end test; the hold-up runners, cramped at the rear and many racing out of their natural position, cannot produce their best finish from a slow pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro controls from the front and the pace is so subdued that he simply outstays a disorganised chasing pack.
scenarios.body: With 16 runners, traffic problems in the straight could prevent hold-up horses from finding a clear run, leaving Montevetro's early advantage intact and his stamina doing the rest on the testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Tired Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the ground rides more yielding than expected and Montevetro's early pace proves costly in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop would help the genuine hold-up horses — Another Day Done and Captain Con — find a clear passage and deliver late, though their redistribution from the rear means positioning problems remain a real risk.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Montevetro fades after setting a muddling pace and a prominent racer pounces early in the straight.
scenarios.body: Chairmanforlife or Misty Cove, tracking close to the pace throughout, would benefit most if the leader ties up and rivals from deep cannot get competitive in time.

watchPoints.text: We're Out Of Aces and Wills History are both Gordon Elliott/McMahon-trained debutants with no public form — monitor market moves in the 30-minute ring, as stable support could signal one of these is significantly better than the field on home evidence.

Montevetro is the only confirmed front-runner in a 16-horse field; if he is slow away or taken on early by an unknown debutant, the entire pace map breaks down and the race becomes genuinely unpredictable.

Camp Verde, Another Day Done, and Bell Ex Too are all natural hold-up horses who will be squeezed wide and forward in a big field — watch for traffic incidents on the first bend as 16 runners sort themselves out.

Matada has been off 111 days and is trained by Gavin Cromwell, who also runs Misty Cove and Neon Eyes in the same race — monitor which of the three stable runners gets the clearest market support as a guide to intent.
Step By Step debuts in a hood for Aidan Anthony Howard, whose yard has a 1/2 T14 record — a small but active stable angle worth noting if any drifting or support appears pre-race.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Brave Lady
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form in this company with three seconds in a four-run recent sequence; Peter Fahey angle is solid but T14 of 0/8 gives slight pause — naturally a front-runner who will need to find space in a crowded prominent group in a field this size.

runners_data.name: The Dotski
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner returning after 195 days off the track, which is a significant fitness query; two hurdle runs at Leopardstown show progression but the layoff and modest recent form string of 54 make this a speculative proposition.

runners_data.name: Goodgollymissholly
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott sends a mare with a hurdle win to her name at 16f on Good ground, which is promising form — however she is a natural front-runner who will likely be pressed wide and back from her preferred spot by the sheer volume of prominent types in this field, diluting her chance.

runners_data.name: Rosarian
runners_data.note: OR 97 with a second over 19f on Good ground as the highlight; Josh Halley stable has been ticking at 1/6 over 14 days and the step back from the Naas Listed effort may suit, though Going to Yielding is untested over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Lunar Majesty
runners_data.note: Seven career hurdle runs without a win and a consistency of mid-pack finishes around 5-6; C A Murphy has no runners in the past 14 days and this mare's best run came third over 20f on Soft, suggesting the trip and going could help marginally.

runners_data.name: Maximillian Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with an eye-catching second at 16f on Soft ground in her form string; returning from 88 days off and the last run ended in a pull-up, raising fitness and jumping confidence questions that need resolving.

runners_data.name: Katie Can't Count
runners_data.note: Mullins runner with only two runs to her name including a fall, making assessment difficult; labelled as a natural prominent racer but the packed field means she is highly unlikely to secure that position, and with no win from two starts confidence is limited.

runners_data.name: Ronnie's Rascal
runners_data.note: OR 104 and the highest-rated runner in the field; four hurdle runs show a consistent placed record including a second over 22f on Good ground — the Mullins/Cleary-Farrell(7) booking is notable and this trip at Ballinrobe suits his profile.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Doyen
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with one relevant hurdle run showing a fourth on Good ground; the age and modest recent form string including pulled-up runs make this a difficult case, though a genuine mid-division style means no early trouble.

runners_data.name: Lexenna
runners_data.note: Three hurdle runs all finishing sixth or below without any placed effort; Darren Collins stable at 0/2 in 14 days and no jockey listed is a flag — hard to make a case for inclusion in the finish.

runners_data.name: Tara Boe
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old returning 16 days after an eighth on Good ground over 20f; hurdling headgear flagged and the form string shows a pulled-up run which raises jumping reliability concerns at this course and trip.

runners_data.name: Santa Paula
runners_data.note: Two thirds in hurdle form at 18f and 16f on Good ground make this mare consistent if unspectacular; OR 99 gives a reasonable class anchor and the Ballinrobe track, which favours handy types who jump well, could suit her staying profile.

runners_data.name: Certosa
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a second at 16f on Good ground as the standout piece of form; seven of eight career runs on Good-side going confirms the surface is right, and OR 99 suggests she is competitive, though a fall in recent form is noted.

runners_data.name: Mia In Milan
runners_data.note: Three hurdle runs all in the lower half of the field including a 13th; the 94-day absence and stable with no recent runners leaves plenty of questions unanswered before this 18-runner test.

runners_data.name: Kilbarry Alexy
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner — absent 251 days and career best a third at 17f on Heavy; the sole leader in a field this size gives her tactical relevance far beyond her raw form, but fitness after a long break is the central concern.

runners_data.name: Sea Limit
runners_data.note: Two runs both resulting in ninths on Good ground; no jockey declared and the stable at 0/0 over 14 days — hard to identify any positive angle and this appears to be a low-expectation entry.

runners_data.name: Mastertown Miss
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard selection at medium confidence; four-year-old with a second at 16f on Soft ground as the best run, and T14 of 2/12 shows the Kelly yard is placing horses with some intent — hold-up style suits the expected race shape.

runners_data.name: Carleys Lilly
runners_data.note: OR 92 with a consistent recent record of placed runs including thirds at 18f on Good ground twice; five career runs all on Good ground confirms the surface suits and Alan O'Sullivan's claim helps weight-wise in a competitive field.

races.paceDynamic: Kilbarry Alexy is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, with 251 days off the track and modest form figures of 39, is unlikely to be pushing a blistering gallop — this points to a sustainable, single-paced lead that keeps the field bunched and the race relatively honest rather than truly searching. Behind Kilbarry Alexy, a cluster of prominent types — Brave Lady, Goodgollymissholly, Katie Can't Count, The Dotski, Rosarian, and Ronnie's Rascal — will be competing for the handful of early positions that actually exist on Ballinrobe's tight track, creating a compressed, convoy-style race shape through the early stages. This field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than the shape can accommodate; of those, Brave Lady and Ronnie's Rascal are best placed to actually secure a forward position given their demonstrated tactical speed, while Goodgollymissholly and Katie Can't Count are most likely to be shuffled back against their nature. A steady pace through the early stages followed by a genuine test from three out on Good to Yielding ground will suit hold-up horses with stamina and a clean passage — the tactical verdict is that closers and mid-to-late movers on a true jumping line have the structural edge here, provided the prominent battle doesn't implode and gift the race to whoever leads.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy sets a steady pace and the prominent scrummage burns energy early, allowing a late challenge from off the pace.
scenarios.body: The compressed field and contested prominent positions mean those further back carry less mid-race pressure and arrive with energy intact at the final two hurdles; Good to Yielding ground rewards genuine stamina over raw speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Brave Lady Stalks And Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Brave Lady secures a clean prominent position just off Kilbarry Alexy and travels through the race without being crowded out.
scenarios.body: Peter Fahey's mare has consistent placed form at this level and handles this going well, and from a position just behind the pace she can dictate her own race without the dangers of the early bunching; a smooth jumping display would see her hit the front at the second-last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Runs Free
scenarios.trigger: If Kilbarry Alexy finds no pressure from the prominent group and is allowed to dictate completely unchallenged at a true gallop.
scenarios.body: A single uncontested leader on a tight track can steal a decisive advantage if the pace behind is too busy sorting out positions; the sustained gallop then tests stamina severely and exposes any hold-up horses that lack a turn of foot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Produces Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses or multiple fallers disrupt the field, producing a grinding test where mid-division horses with clean jumping benefit.
scenarios.body: A scrambled, slow-burn race on softening ground at Ballinrobe can see the race only fully ignite from three out, rewarding those who jump fluently and improve late; those from a genuine midfield base avoid the prominent scrimmage entirely.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Brave Lady or Ronnie's Rascal can actually secure a prominent position at the off — if both are crowded out, the projected race shape shifts dramatically toward a cleaner race for hold-up horses.

Kilbarry Alexy's fitness after 251 days on the sidelines is the critical pace question — if she fades quickly after the first circuit, the race loses its only pace anchor and becomes a bunched sprint from three out.

Katie Can't Count's fall in recent form and Tara Boe's pulled-up run both raise jumping safety concerns in an 18-runner field on Ballinrobe's tight track — fallers from prominent positions could cause significant interference.

Mastertown Miss is drawn in a hold-up role in a race the pace map suggests will suit that profile — watch how cleanly Peter Smithers (5) navigates the early bunching through the first mile, as a clear passage is essential to her chance.

Goodgollymissholly has the Gordon Elliott win on the board and genuine ability, but if she is unable to replicate her natural front-running style and is forced to race in traffic from a midfield base, her chance is structurally compromised from the gate.

runners_data.name: Take The Free
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a win over 20f on Good ground and a recent runner-up on Soft; E Bolger's 1/4 trainer form over 14 days is a minor positive, and 67 days off is manageable given his in-form profile over trips shorter than today's 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Crossing The Bar
runners_data.note: Has not run in 523 days — a 17-month absence makes this entirely unknown territory; lightly raced and unrated on going in similar conditions, caution is essential despite the ability shown in a 2021 form string that contained a win.

runners_data.name: Mickey Cohen
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a win over 18f on Good and placed efforts at 20f and 24f in similar conditions; Noel Meade's yard is cold (1/32 over 14 days) but the horse's own form figures of 1-2-3 in the recent string are compelling for this trip and surface.

runners_data.name: Luck Between Us
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator who has won over 20f on Good and finished second over this exact 2m6f trip recently — the best course-and-distance profile among the closers; Niall Moore's 5lb claim helps offset the welter weight, and 23 days since last run is ideal.

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has placed twice from five outings on Good ground, including a second over 22f most recently; the 5lb claim of Alan O'Sullivan keeps the weight manageable at OR 116, and he is the Scorecard's primary danger — his stamina at this trip is his key asset.

runners_data.name: Better Times
runners_data.note: Recorded his only win on Soft over 22f, which gives some going affinity, but his true running style is as a hold-up horse and with several closers in this field he will struggle to find the clear run from deep that he needs; 104 days between runs is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Mr Dibbs
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner and the pace-setter on whom every scenario pivots; won over 2m2f on Good 13 days ago for Gavin Cromwell, wears a hood, and is lightly weighted at OR 101 — his ability to control tempo is the race's central question.

runners_data.name: Strange Currency
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up racer by nature but shifted forward on the map due to the congestion of closers; his recent form figures show consistent mediocrity on Good ground and no wins in eight similar-going runs, making it hard to see him threatening even if he finds his preferred position.

runners_data.name: Arcland
runners_data.note: The Scorecard's top selection — a hold-up horse who won over 20f on Good and placed over 18f in his last two starts; wears a hood for Gavin Cromwell and at age 10 his stamina at 2m6f is his weapon, though his recent last-two form shows a fifth and a 10th after the win, needing everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Ehteyat
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner in the field at OR 121 but has pulled up most recently and his form figures on Good ground show an alarming deterioration; prominent style suits the anticipated shape but the P on debut for M K Flannery (0/0 14-day) demands caution.

runners_data.name: Free Flow
runners_data.note: A natural closer whose last five runs show finishes of 4th, 6th, 11th, 9th, and 11th — no wins across seven similar-going outings and no placed efforts; ran just 7 days ago which raises a fitness question and his position on the map is a product of redistribution, not genuine style.

runners_data.name: In The Minus
runners_data.note: Young hold-up horse who won over 21f on Good and placed over 20f on the same surface — strong stamina form for a 4-year-old; 23 days since last run and Shane Fitzgerald's booking is straightforward; the trip and going tick, but the class ceiling is uncertain at OR 116.

runners_data.name: Pilgrims Walk
runners_data.note: A natural closer by style but, being a redistributed horse in this shape, is less likely to get the true rear position needed to deliver a big finish; his back-to-back placed efforts over 22-24f on Good ground are form-relevant, and a 3lb claim from Shane O'Callaghan partially offsets the penalty.

runners_data.name: Needs Must
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner has been off 178 days and his last outing was a fall; his one win came on Soft over 20f which suits the going angle, and a prominent style is well suited to the expected shape — but the long layoff and mid-race fall last time make him a speculative proposition at best.

races.paceDynamic: Mr Dibbs is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him early over 2m6f on Good To Yielding ground at Ballinrobe, he is likely to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — his recent Goodwood win at this trip confirms he can travel well off his own pace. Behind him, Take The Free, Mickey Cohen, and Ehteyat will look to press or track prominently, creating a second tier of mid-pace stalkers rather than genuine pressers. The field holds more true hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Better Times, Strange Currency, Free Flow, and Pilgrims Walk are all natural closers but are likely to find themselves racing closer to midfield than ideal given the shuffling effect of 14 runners and a modest gallop. A controlled pace set by Mr Dibbs over a stamina trip on this softening ground will compress the field in the middle stages, meaning the race is unlikely to truly develop until the final turn — this shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with stamina and late acceleration, rather than pure hold-up finishers who need a strong pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs sets a sustainable rhythm unchallenged and the race only ignites approaching the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: Mr Dibbs' contained gallop keeps the field bunched into the straight, where horses just off the pace — prominent and mid-division — have the energy reserves to pounce late; the Good To Yielding surface rewards those who have travelled efficiently rather than ground through heavy early sectionals.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Dibbs is allowed to dictate fully and kicks for home before the final flight, stealing a decisive advantage.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to close him down through the race, Mr Dibbs converts his controlled lead into a winning one by stretching clear in the straight when his rivals are flat-footed; his recent course-compatible win over this exact trip underlines his ability to see it out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely muddling and those in the first four lengths at the top of the straight have a decisive positional advantage.
scenarios.body: Take The Free and Mickey Cohen, both carrying good recent form on similar going, are ideally placed to capitalise if the race develops into a tactical scramble where tracking the leader beats chasing from behind; Ehteyat's top-rated OR of 121 could see him find rhythm from a prominent berth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver From Deep
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow quickens sharply early, stringing the field out and generating genuine back-straight fractions that reward true hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: This scenario is discounted because Better Times, Strange Currency, Free Flow, and Pilgrims Walk are all redistributed away from the rear — they are unlikely to get their natural closing position and will not be able to produce a vintage hold-up finish; Arcland and Luck Between Us, as the most legitimate deep-finishers with genuine stamina form, are best placed if this shape unexpectedly materialises.

watchPoints.text: Arcland (Scorecard top) was 10th and 5th in the two runs before a recent comeback — watch whether Eoghan Finegan can get him into a good rhythm from the hold-up berth early, as a bunched midfield could trap him.

Mr Dibbs is a 7-year-old front-runner with a hood, ridden by a 7lb claimer (Alix Balfe) — if Balfe allows the gallop to quicken too sharply on the Good To Yielding, Mr Dibbs could hit the wall turning in and hand the race to hold-up horses.

Jupiter Du Gite has placed twice on Good ground but Alan O'Sullivan (5lb) has limited experience at this level — watch whether he can manoeuvre the horse into a position to challenge at the second-last without getting blocked in a 14-runner field.

Needs Must (Gordon Elliott) is 178 days absent after a fall — watch for any signs of hesitation at the early hurdles, as a reluctant jumper could unsettle several horses immediately behind in a big field.

Ehteyat (OR 121, highest-rated) is a prominent type whose last run was a pull-up — if he bounces back in the first half of the race and forces an unexpectedly fast early pace, it would significantly alter the scenario probabilities in favour of hold-up finishers.

runners_data.name: Cobra Queen
runners_data.note: Proven on Good ground with a strong sim-going record of 1W3P across six runs; the confirmed front-runner here who carries the blinkers and is expected to dictate, though her style-fit tag at 0.92 is a mild caveat if pressed earlier than ideal.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with no wins or places from five sim-going runs — a persistently frustrating profile; rides out of the prominent position but has consistently disappointed, and the 3/27 trainer strike rate in the last 14 days offers no particular confidence boost.

runners_data.name: Theflyingbee
runners_data.note: Consistent placer who has finished second or third four times in last six sim-going starts; the nine-year-old tracks prominently and handles Good ground well over this trip, making her an honest each-way type if conditions stay in range.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: Recent course-distance winner on Good ground for Ross O'Sullivan, and the booking of a 7lb claimer in Shane Markey keeps the weight competitive at 149lbs; midfield in style, she is one of the more interesting runners if the pace is honest enough.

runners_data.name: Sound Judgement
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner who won over 2m4f on Good ground and has placed three times in seven sim-going starts; sits close to the pace from a prominent position and the Good-to-Soft at Ballinrobe should not inconvenience her.

runners_data.name: Nothing Hectic
runners_data.note: Won over 2m2f on Good ground and has a genuine hold-up profile that gives her a tactical chance if the race is truly run; Ricky Doyle rides a horse who needs things to unfold naturally from the rear over this stamina test.

runners_data.name: St Anthonys Corner
runners_data.note: Returned from a 345-day absence and has a flagged tendency to fade in the finish — her single sim-going run produced an 11th-place finish, and her profile suggests she is unlikely to threaten at this level on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Run For The Border
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with four places from nine sim-going runs who carries a style-fit discount; placed over 2m6f on Good ground last time out, but the redistribution to midfield means she may not get the race run that fully suits her true closer's game.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: In-form mare who has placed eight times in twelve sim-going runs and is the Strand Scorecard's top selection despite being a true hold-up runner; the redistribution means she is unlikely to get the ideal waiting position, and the 0.93 style-fit flag tempers confidence, but her raw form figures are the most compelling in the race.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Harry Sexton (7) aboard a mare who has placed once from four sim-going runs; a hold-up profile that has produced a second over 2m on Good ground, but she has not previously tackled 2m6f and the trip query is real.

runners_data.name: She'll Be Kept
runners_data.note: Two course-distance wins including most recently over 2m4f on Good ground makes this a fascinating closer; Mr E M Nugent (7) takes the mount and while the amateur angle is a watch point, the form and profile over this trip and going are the most proven of any hold-up runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Cobra Queen is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to press her from the off, she should be able to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over 2m6f of Good to Yielding ground at Ballinrobe. Camlin Park, Theflyingbee and Sound Judgement will track closely in a prominent cluster, ensuring the early fractions are not dawdled, but none carries the profile to seize the lead from Cobra Queen. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — You Make Me Smile and Run For The Border are both true closers who will likely find themselves racing closer to midfield than their natural position, which dilutes the advantage they would ordinarily carry; She'll Be Kept and Nothing Hectic are the purest hold-up runners in the field. A controlled, honest pace over a genuine stamina trip on cut ground suits resolute, thorough stayers who can travel prominently or grind from the rear — a race shape that points firmly towards hold-up types with proven stamina and towards the front-runner Cobra Queen if the pace proves truly undemanding.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cobra Queen Dictates Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Cobra Queen bowls along in front at a controlled clip and the prominent pack fails to mount a serious sustained challenge before the last.
scenarios.body: Cobra Queen settles into her rhythm on a track where she handles the ground well, and with no horse possessing the boot to decisively close on a confirmed front-runner at a fair pace, she times her effort to repel late challengers; Sound Judgement from a prominent position is best placed to chase her down.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves honest enough to stretch the field and the closers get a truly run race over this stamina-sapping trip.
scenarios.body: She'll Be Kept, a winner twice in similar conditions and over this sort of trip, has the profile to pick up the pieces late, and Nothing Hectic, a genuine hold-up type who won over 2m2f in Good ground, could also emerge from off the pace as tiring rivals drop away.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Overhauled
scenarios.trigger: If Cobra Queen's early advantage is eroded by a prominent pressing group and the race degenerates into a slog from three out.
scenarios.body: Theflyingbee has the consistency and course-suitable profile to excel when a race is run at a true gallop that suits thorough stayers, having placed repeatedly in similar conditions; Sound Judgement, with a win over 2m4f in Good ground, has the stamina to see it out from a tracking position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Pace
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners break their cover or jockey errors disrupt the expected shape, creating a ragged, stop-start pace.
scenarios.body: In a muddled race where the pace is uneven, Walkingmayotomilan's recent course-distance win and relatively light weight could make her dangerous from midfield, while Bossy Bird could benefit from an unconventional tempo that neutralises the proven front-runner.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Cobra Queen faces any early pressure from Camlin Park or Theflyingbee — if those prominent types crowd her into a faster early pace than she seeks, her chance of controlling the race diminishes sharply.

She'll Be Kept's amateur rider Mr E M Nugent (7) is a factor to monitor — if he misjudges the hold-up tactics on a mare who has won twice from off the pace, her proven stamina advantage could be wasted.

You Make Me Smile is a true closer mapped to midfield because of the field's composition — watch whether Sean Cleary-Farrell (7) can manoeuvre her into a position at the rear that gives her any chance of producing a sustained late run.
Run For The Border ran just 11 days ago for John Patrick Ryan, making her the freshest recent runner; watch for any signs of fatigue in the latter stages over this stamina-testing 2m6f trip.

St Anthonys Corner's 345-day absence and the flagged finishing fade make her worth tracking early — if she is struggling before the home turn, it confirms the race is likely to be contested by the main pace figures and classier closers.

races.paceDynamic: Affinity Rock is the one confirmed front-runner in a field of nine and, with no genuine rival willing or able to press from the gate, should find a comfortable, uncontested lead on Good To Yielding ground that suits her recent form. Behind her, a cluster of prominent-minded runners — Giorgia Rose, Joya Del Mar, Survivors Sister, and Straight Home — will jostle for the positions immediately off the pace, creating meaningful congestion between the second and third-last fences where traffic incidents become a real risk. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the shape can accommodate: Cherry Red and Carried With Love are both natural prominent racers but have been mapped to midfield as they are unlikely to secure their preferred berth, meaning they race at a disadvantage to their true style. With Affinity Rock dictating a sustainable, uncontested rhythm and the middle-pack crowded, this race shape strongly favours a single prominent-tracking horse who can sit just off the leader, avoid the congestion, and mount a clean challenge from two out — making the nearest-to-lead prominent profile the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Affinity Rock Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Affinity Rock leads unchallenged and the pack behind fights for prominence, leaving her fresh for the final climb.
scenarios.body: Affinity Rock slips into a metronomic rhythm with no rival applying pressure, conserving energy through the Good To Yielding ground before kicking on from two out; runners behind her get tangled in the prominent scrum and cannot close the gap in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If one clean-tracking prominent horse avoids the midfield traffic and reels in a tiring Affinity Rock after the last.
scenarios.body: A prominent runner positioned just off Affinity Rock's shoulder throughout gets a clean run when the leader begins to empty, arriving with momentum at the final fence; the Good To Yielding ground rewards those who have settled rather than scrapped for position in the early stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrum collapses the pace and the field strings out, creating a gap for a hold-up horse to come through.
scenarios.body: Cooke's Lass or Ad Caelum, racing away from the early traffic, find clear daylight as the race quickens from three out; the stamina-sapping distance on softening ground plays to their staying profile if the pace has been genuinely honest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Group Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes interference two-three out and reshuffles the race entirely from an unexpected position.
scenarios.body: A melee between Giorgia Rose, Joya Del Mar and Survivors Sister at the penultimate fence scrambles the finishing order and opens the door for a runner who has threaded clear; the beneficiary is likely whoever has avoided the trouble rather than the horse with the classiest profile.

watchPoints.text: Watch for early scrimmaging between Giorgia Rose, Joya Del Mar, Survivors Sister and Straight Home jumping off — with four horses wanting prominent ground behind Affinity Rock, the first two fences could see sharp positional battles that unsettle one or more.

Cooke's Lass returning after 364 days is a significant layoff risk — if she is not fully wound up, a blunder or lack of fluency at any fence could compromise not just her run but any runner tracking close behind.

Cherry Red and Carried With Love, forced to race behind their natural position, are worth tracking from the back of the prominent group — if a gap opens on the far side at the third-last they may arrive with unexpected momentum, making them dangerous at a price.

Affinity Rock's claimer Carl Millar has not ridden this horse before; in a race she otherwise controls, any jumping error under an unfamiliar partner at the open ditch could instantly change the complexion of the race.

The Good To Yielding ground is confirmed by the going report for this 2m7f trip — stamina will be tested, and runners with proven form at this distance on similar going (Joya Del Mar, Ad Caelum) hold a meaningful edge over those stepping up in trip for the first time.

races.paceDynamic: Kilashee is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and will set out to control this 2m7f contest from the front, but the fades-in-finish flag is a significant concern over this extended trip on Good to Yielding ground — he is likely to set an honest rather than scorching gallop, keeping the tempo sustainable and the field compact. Fr Gilligansvoyge, Hit The Frame, Las Brisas Boy and Reve Inoui are genuine prominent types who will push forward behind him, meaning there will be a well-populated front group that collectively ensures the pace is real without being suicidal. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than the map can accommodate: The Little Yank, U Asking Me, Swing Time and Set The Tone are all natural hold-up horses who will be competing for rear-to-midfield positions they may not fully secure in a field this large, making their redistribution to midfield a structural inevitability rather than a tactical choice. A genuine, honest gallop on soft-leaning ground over nearly three miles with a confirmed front-runner who fades late strongly favours horses who travel smoothly in the second half of the field, produce a sustained jump-by-jump challenge from the home turn and have the proven class to pick off a tiring leader — the late-pressing hold-up profile is the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee sets a genuine but sustainable gallop that strings the field out and leaves him vulnerable from three out.
scenarios.body: Kilashee's known tendency to fade in the finish means the well-held hold-up runners can close the gap methodically over the final mile, with the Good to Yielding ground rewarding stamina over speed; horses with strong sim-going records and clean jumping profiles will arrive full of running at the last. Ladies Well, with eight from eight on similar going and back-to-back wins, is ideally placed to pounce, while Mistyburn and Il Silenzio have the class and jumping to finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Group Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners — Fr Gilligansvoyge, Las Brisas Boy, Hit The Frame — push forward aggressively and one secures a clean lead with Kilashee fading out of contention.
scenarios.body: A horse who travels prominently throughout and conserves energy by avoiding early scrimmaging will be ideally suited, as the mid-race pace from a settled front group on testing ground rewards those with class and accuracy at their fences. Fr Gilligansvoyge's exceptional record of 3W7P from 12 runs, all on Good ground, makes the prominent profile dangerous here if he gets a smooth passage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Kilashee's tendency to fade kicks in earlier than expected and the prominent horses set too strong an early tempo, causing a bunched late finish.
scenarios.body: Genuine hold-up horses who are able to secure their natural position at the rear — Island McCoo and Mistyburn, who are not redistributed — will find the scenario plays directly into their hands as others run themselves into the ground. Mistyburn's ten from fourteen on similar going and Island McCoo's course-experience and winning form at the trip make both dangerous if the race truly falls apart up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Attrition Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the large 19-runner field produces jumping errors, fallers or interference that disrupts the natural running order and the race becomes a test of pure jumping accuracy.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners over fences on Good to Yielding ground, safely-jumped, straightforward horses that avoid trouble will be at a premium — runners with poor recent form strings (P, U, F) make this scenario live. Set The Tone's consistent placed form and clean-jumping history give it residual interest, but Ladies Well's positive sim-going record and young age means she is one of the least likely to be found out.

watchPoints.text: Kilashee's fade flag is the central tactical fulcrum of this race — watch whether he weakens approaching the third-last, as his capitulation will determine whether closers like Ladies Well and Mistyburn get a clean run at the leaders or must navigate a falling leader.

Fr Gilligansvoyge is 13 years old and has an exceptional record at this track and trip — if he travels prominently and jumps cleanly at the top of the hill, he could steal a march on the hold-up horses who may not close the gap in time over this course configuration.

With 19 runners over fences on Good to Yielding ground, the early fences will be chaotic — watch for interference or jumping errors among the redistributed midfield cluster (The Little Yank, U Asking Me, Swing Time, Set The Tone) who will be competing for positions they would not naturally occupy.

Il Silenzio carries the top weight of 168lbs at OR 100 — if he travels easily despite the burden and the pace is honest, he has the class to win this race, but watch whether Conor Smithers can ride a patient race from hold-up given the weight.

Trainer John Patrick Ryan saddles three runners (Kilashee, Zolpharine, The Little Yank) and is 2/14 in the past 14 days — watch market moves on all three as stable intelligence may indicate which runner

runners_data.name: Bossing It
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has posted a place effort (2/17f on similar ground) — David O'Brien runner likely to creep into the race late from the back, but 0W1P from five similar-going runs suggests he may lack the finishing kick to win.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Joint-top weight, in-form front-runner who won 14 days ago for Hanlon; pace headgear confirms role, and 2W2P on 11 similar-going runs underline class, but carrying 166lbs against two rivals also intent on leading is a serious energy drain.

runners_data.name: Lady Doyanne

runners_data.name: Fedneys Park

runners_data.name: Feet On The Ground

runners_data.name: Poppycon
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has placed twice over 20f on good-to-yielding — cheekpieces and tongue strap add focus; the fall on his form card is a jumping concern in a 19-runner field over fences, though his 0W3P placed record shows he can compete.

runners_data.name: Coole Vision
runners_data.note: Lowly-rated 9yo for Norman Lee at 0/4 over 14 days with just two similar-going runs on the form card and no wins or places; hard to make a case in a wide-open competitive field.

races.paceDynamic: Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude are all confirmed front-runners in a 19-runner field, and they will contest the early lead aggressively on good-to-yielding ground around Ballinrobe's tight circuit, guaranteeing a genuine gallop from the off. With eight of nineteen runners wanting prominent positions, the early furlongs will see significant jostling and crowding, particularly turning into the back straight, with traffic danger intensifying between the second-last and last fence as that prominent cluster concertinas. The strong pace set by three genuine leaders will stretch the field and burn off horses carrying big weights who lack the class to sustain the tempo — this is a stamina examination, not a tactical race. A sustained gallop on this ground over 2m1f emphatically favours hold-up horses with proven stamina and the ability to thread through late traffic, rewarding horses who can be produced with one clean run from the back of the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude burn each other out setting a fierce pace and the front group cries enough from 3 out.
scenarios.body: The three leaders set a punishing gallop that exhausts the prominent pack, opening a clear lane for hold-up horses sweeping from midfield to late; good-to-yielding ground rewards genuine stamina over raw speed, meaning those who travel within themselves into the straight hold the decisive edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Mo Ghille Mar controls the fractions and the two rivals Leave In Secret and Claude are forced to race off his pace without getting competitive.
scenarios.body: Mo Ghille Mar, trained by Hanlon and in good recent form with a win 14 days ago, has the class and course-appropriate profile to slot comfortably at the head of affairs and find enough to hold on if the pace is not truly brutal; a top-weight burden slows the closers on this stamina-testing circuit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not ruinous, allowing prominent horses who settle just off the lead to pounce turning for home while the pure leaders weaken.
scenarios.body: Horses like Farrokh, Stoneyford Lady, Lady Doyanne, and Phoenix Arizona — all natural prominent types with solid good-ground form — are positioned to exploit any slight slackening of the suicidal early pace and pick off the spent leaders; Lady Doyanne's consistent placed record and Stoneyford Lady's De Bromhead sharpness make them the likeliest to benefit in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Unravels, Chaos Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes interference, fallers, or significant traffic problems from 3 out leaving a messy finish.
scenarios.body: With 19 runners, a strong pace, and prominent congestion flagged between the second-last and last, incident is plausible; any horse lucky enough to find a clear passage late regardless of style could grab a position, though form figures suggest Ballybrittas or Poppycon could benefit from the chaos if their midfield berths avoid the trouble.

watchPoints.text: Mo Ghille Mar, Leave In Secret, and Claude will contest the early lead — watch for a pace war inside the first half mile that could compromise all three and open the race for hold-up horses.

With eight prominent runners in a 19-runner field, severe traffic congestion is forecast between the second-last and last fence — horses on the inner could be badly hampered; jockeys on Le Diablo and Sayitfirst must find clear routes early.

Claude carries a tongue tie and breast girth suggesting jumping or wind concerns; if he makes a jumping error under pressure at the head of a 19-runner field, the consequences for runners close behind could be serious.

Le Diablo is the Strand Scorecard selection but is rated low confidence — the hold-up style is perfectly placed for this pace shape, but in a 19-runner handicap at this level the difference between winning and unplaced can be one blocked passage from 3 out.

Trainer Henry De Bromhead runs three horses (Stoneyford Lady, Lady Doyanne, Fedneys Park) — the yard is in strong 4/26 form over 14 days; watch for which one receives the stronger ride as that may indicate stable confidence.
